newsitem.title: USA: Weyerhaeuser sees Q2 plant closing charge.
newsitem.headline: Weyerhaeuser sees Q2 plant closing charge.

text.p: Weyerhaeuser Co said it it plans to close its Plymouth Plywood plant in North Carolina, resulting in a charge against its second quarter earnings.

A spokesman said that while the amount of the charge was as yet undetermined, it would be more than offset by the company's sale of its Weyerhaeuaser Mortgage Co to WMC Acquisition Co for $192 million on May 22.
In a statement, Weyerhaeuser said the closure is part of its long-term strategy to align its wood product manufacturing facilities with changing future sources of raw material.

It added it is closing the plant rather than modernizing due to market conditions and high raw material values. In addition, the plant lacks an independent energy source, a problem also requiring a substantial investment, it said.
Weyerhaeuser, an integrated forest products company, said it is examining opportunities to modernize existing North Carolina lumber operations.
